items.title: Shame and fear forcing international visitors to become Australia's new homeless generation
items.description: A man dies. His body is not noticed for nearly a week. He was invisible to many, like the growing number of homeless Australia wide.

items.title: UK leaders call for calm after asylum seeker arrested over Belfast stabbing
items.description: Protesters hold anti-immigration demonstrations in Northern Ireland and England after a Sudanese man is arrested over a "brutal" knife attack in Belfast.

items.title: Live: US military launches strikes on Iran after helicopter downing
items.description: The US has started striking Iran in response to the downing of one of its Apache helicopters, the US Central Command says. Follow live.

items.title: 'Beside him until the last moment': Father mourns baby shot by Israeli troops
items.description: A Palestinian father promises to fight for justice for his seven-month-old son, who was shot dead by an Israeli soldier in the West Bank city of Hebron.

items.title: Thirteen government agencies embroiled in potential data breach
items.description: Thirteen government agencies are now embroiled in an expanding scandal involving potential data breaches prompting calls for an urgent audit amid concerns over national security.

items.title: Why was Rolf Harris never tried for his crimes in Australia?
items.description: Rolf Harris's conviction for child sexual abuse was shocking to those who saw him as a lovable larrikin. But the people who were abused by him are refusing to stay silent about the impacts of his crimes.

items.title: Live: Tony Abbott says his government was a 'let-down' to many Liberals
items.description: Former prime minister Tony Abbott has told a book launch in Washington that his government was a "let-down" to many Liberals. Follow live.

items.title: How police may have inadvertently saved this man from Ivan Milat
items.description: Etched in Steven Clark's memory are the protruding teeth and moustache of the driver he says picked him up as a teenager — a man he now believes was serial killer Ivan Milat.

items.title: Is Australia sucking the joy out of childhood?
items.description: The first time Renae Powell waved her eldest child through the primary school gates she felt something was missing: playtime.

items.title: These cranes are battery-powered as firms increasingly ditch diesel
items.description: The Iran war and the oil supply squeeze are supercharging business investment in renewables.

items.title: Why Xi Jinping made an exception to see Kim Jong Un in person
items.description: Xi Jinping and Kim Jong Un's bilateral talks in North Korea were a big departure from the Chinese president's usual diplomacy playbook because, for this first time this year, he was the one travelling abroad to make the meeting happen.

items.title: When does the FIFA World Cup start and who are the favourites?
items.description: The FIFA World Cup is the biggest single-sport event on the planet and has delivered numerous historical moments, from Diego Maradona's "hand of God" in 1986 to Zinedine Zidane's infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi.

items.title: Five mattresses on the floor as families wait months for repairs
items.description: Delays in maintenance repairs, including mould removal, are forcing families to sleep on mattresses in living rooms, adding to overcrowding pressures in remote homes.

items.title: Serena Williams makes winning return to court at Queen's
items.description: Serena Williams steals the show at Queen's Club, as the American icon marks her eagerly awaited return to competitive action with a doubles victory nearly four years after her last match.

items.title: Finding and saving the world's biggest trees before they disappear
items.description: It took a decade for researchers to find the tallest tree in East Asia. Now they know where the 84.1-metre conifer is but the future of its species and other tall trees is dire.

items.title: Quiz: Stow your luggage in the locker overhead, we're off to see the world
items.description: The lek is the currency of which country? And what's the Japanese word for pufferfish, the sashimi delicacy that's toxic if prepared incorrectly?

items.title: Calling all budding storytellers living with disability
items.description: If you are an emerging content maker or journalist with disability and have a story to tell, now is your chance to work with the ABC to tell it.

items.title: 'Just an absolute tip': Residents frustrated with rise of illegal dumping
items.description: Councils across Melbourne's suburbs are struggling to combat the rise of illegal dumping, despite over $21 million of funding from the Victorian state government.

items.title: Victim-survivors tear up agreement with Catholic church
items.description: Victim-survivors of clergy abuse say negotiations and agreements reached with the Catholic Diocese of Ballarat are now null and void.

items.title: Man found dead in Melbourne park had suffered burns, police say
items.description: Police say the man appeared to have suffered burns and was discovered by a passer-by in parkland in Melbourne's east.

items.title: Shivanya was walking through a mall when five words made her freeze
items.description: A retail worker at Sydney's Broadway Shopping Centre says she was left scared after a man told her he had a knife.

items.title: Gary Ablett Jr joins dad in Australian Football Hall of Fame
items.description: Six new members are inducted into the Australian Football Hall of Fame, including Geelong and Gold Coast legend Gary Ablett Jr.

items.title: How a 'bit of paint' could help relieve overcrowded Brisbane buses
items.description: Buses are Queensland's most popular form of public transport, but advocates say a lack of investment means they are often unreliable and overcrowded.

items.title: Seized greyhounds looked like 'RSPCA cases', kennel owner says
items.description: A dog kennel owner is searching for answers after Greyhound Racing SA put two dogs that appeared malnourished and one with an open wound "you could stick your finger into" in her care. Warning: This article contains images and content that some readers may find distressing.

items.title: Steaks could soon cost more, but restaurants have other ideas
items.description: Red meat is expected to become more expensive starting this month as higher diesel prices have filtered through the supply chain.
